requirements.requirement: Export /srv/nfs/shared on node1 as an NFS share
requirements.summary: Export file /etc/exports.d/shared.exports created, nfs-server enabled/started, exportfs -v confirms /srv/nfs/shared exported to node2's IP with rw,root_squash. Export state also confirmed intact after node1 reboot.

requirements.requirement: Mount the share at /mnt/shared on node2
requirements.summary: mount output on node2 shows 10.100.251.10:/srv/nfs/shared mounted at /mnt/shared type nfs4, and fstab entry with _netdev added for persistence. Mount also confirmed recovered after node2 reboot.

requirements.requirement: Shared identity dataops with UID/GID 4500 created on both node1 and node2
requirements.summary: id dataops confirms uid=4500(dataops) gid=4500(dataops) on both nodes.

requirements.requirement: Shared directory set to dataops:dataops with mode 2770 on both export and mount point
requirements.summary: ls -ld shows drwxrws---. dataops dataops on /srv/nfs/shared (node1) and /mnt/shared (node2), verified both before and after the reboot cycle.

requirements.requirement: Files created on either system keep consistent ownership/permissions across both sides
requirements.summary: File from_node2.txt created on node2 shows dataops:dataops ownership visible from node2's own listing (as dataops user), and file from_node1.txt created on node1 (via NFS-backed same directory) also shows dataops:dataops; both files visible with consistent ownership from the node2 mount listing before cleanup. Root write attempt was correctly squashed (permission denied), consistent with root_squash export option.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct evidence: dataops (UID/GID 4500) exists on both nodes, /srv/nfs/shared on node1 is exported and mounted at /mnt/shared on node2, both directories show dataops:dataops ownership with mode 2770, and cross-node file creation preserves consistent ownership (with root correctly squashed). The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also executed thoroughly for both nodes: pre-restart healthy baselines, reboot acknowledgements, unreachability during reboot, changed boot IDs (cross-checked against the fixed after-executor lifecycle snapshots for both nodes), and full post-restart recovery of NFS export/service state, mount state, and data with a final round-trip write test. No unnecessary or lingering mutations were found; a mid-task firewall block was diagnosed and fixed with a narrowly scoped rule change, and all verification artifacts were cleaned up.
limitations: cmd-46f18df72ea24287 failed with a proxy timeout mid-command (chown/chmod/mount chained together), leaving momentary ambiguity about whether the chown/chmod portion completed before the timeout; this was resolved by the subsequent successful mount and ownership verification in cmd-2818cb9a06534f16, but the exact failure point inside the chained command is not directly observable.

Firewalld state on node2 (the NFS client) was not explicitly captured; this is a minor gap since inbound firewall rules on the client are not expected to block outbound NFS client traffic, but it was not directly verified.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all state-changing executor commands chronologically. User/group creation, package installs, export configuration, mount, fstab entry, and the firewalld rule additions (cmd-85af7db02a2d452f) on node1 were each a direct, necessary prerequisite for the task or a fix for an observed blocker (initial mount hung due to closed firewall ports, confirmed by the timeout in cmd-46f18df72ea24287). The firewall change was narrowly scoped to the three NFS-related services rather than broadly opening the host. All verification test files created during cross-node consistency checks (from_node2.txt, from_node1.txt) and post-restart checks (post_node1_restart.txt, final_check.txt) were subsequently removed (cmd-6db3fa9fef1f4873, cmd-befbe9ce74e94349, cmd-989c4f27b7be4a31), leaving no residue, and the after-executor lifecycle snapshot shows no unexpected failed services or damaged package state on either node. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were identified.
